page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It supplies 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. A key aspect of its hardware profile is the allocation of 1344 GB of RAM, providing a massive 84 GB of memory per vCPU. Cache specifications include 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache per physical topology. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and accelerated cryptography primitives like AES-NI and SHA-NI.

Benchmark assessments reveal top-tier single-threaded compute performance. The server achieved a top-10-percent Geekbench single-core score of 2364.0 and a text processing score of 2950.0. In compression testing, it registered strong single-threaded performance, yielding 34.83 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.28 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance scales predictably across its 16 vCPUs, recording 17775.0 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a multi-core Geekbench score of 13643.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 131.84 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measured 91.25 GB/sec. Small 135M parameter LLM inference achieved text generation speeds of 282.43 tokens per second.

From a hardware design and cost efficiency perspective, the FX64-16ms_v2 prioritizes RAM density over raw vCPU core counts. With 84 GB per vCPU, it eliminates the need to over-provision CPU cores simply to obtain large memory capacity, delivering high resource efficiency for single-thread bound, memory-heavy workloads. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local ephemeral SSD storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, requiring relying entirely on remote storage volumes for operational disk I/O. This instance is optimally suited for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis caches, financial risk simulation models, and memory-intensive data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V with the x86_64 architecture, this instance offers an extraordinary 1344 GB of system memory, resulting in 84 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and VAES encryption. Benchmark results highlight top-tier Geekbench single-core execution and text processing scores, along with strong single-threaded gzip compression speed of 34.83 GB/sec. No GPU hardware or local ephemeral storage is bundled, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent disk needs. The extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio offers distinct cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads that do not require massive CPU core scale. This server configuration is best suited for large in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, high-memory data analytics, and memory-constrained text processing or LLM inference tasks.
